label: copy-phase input token t (fed-back t, not the first copied token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is the letter t, at recall_idx >= 2 (i.e., the t being re-read is original token 1 or later). It never fires on any other input token, never in the original or delimiter phase, and is almost silent when t is the first copied token (recall_idx 1, 0.2% of mass). Roughly 86% of qualifying steps are active. In the top and bottom examples, magnitude is largest when the t comes late in the copy, near the end of the sequence (top examples have t as the last or second-to-last copy input), and smallest when t is copied early (recall_idx 2-3). When two t inputs come in a row, the second one is usually weaker or inactive. Output token, sequence length and digit count barely change the firing rate.

issues: I reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.858, R 0.994, F1 0.921, mass recall 0.998. The feature is completely silent in the original and delimiter phases and on every input token except t (profile: all 64615 dev activations have in_tok=t and are in the copy phase).

Steps where t is the first copied token (recall_idx 1) carry only 0.2% of the mass (404 active). The predicate misses 376 test steps holding 0.2% of the mass, and most of those are this recall_idx-1 case, at activations of 0.01-0.12 of max. That is negligible.

The 10542 test false positives (about 14% of predicted steps) are spread out rather than forming one class. Firing rate within the predicate: to_go 0-5 gives 0.83-0.89, to_go>=6 gives 0.77, recall_idx 2 gives 0.74, in_count>=2 gives 0.76, orig(0)==t gives 0.66, L==3 gives 0.29 (only 430 steps), n_digits>=3 gives 0.95, out_tok==t gives 0.99. The only strong suppressor is prev_tok==t (rate 0.41 on 2440 steps). Excluding it gives test F1 0.922, versus 0.921 without the exclusion, so leaving it out is reasonable. The explanation already mentions it.

The magnitude claim holds up when I derive it from the profile (mass share divided by active count): mean activation per active step rises with recall_idx, from about 1.06e-5 per step at recall_idx 2 to 1.55e-5 at recall_idx 3 and 1.89e-5 at recall_idx 8. Copies late in the sequence are stronger.
